## Problem Introduction

COVID-19 significantly disrupted the global entertainment industry, affecting film production, cinema attendance, and consumer viewing habits.

As audiences increasingly turned to streaming services during lockdowns, Netflix experienced changes in both content production and revenue performance.

This study investigates how Netflix film budgets, revenues, and release volumes changed before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic.

## Research Question

How did Netflix film budgets and revenues change before, during and after COVID-19?

## Dataset Description

### Dataset Overview

- Public Netflic film dataset
- Approximately 16,000 movie records
- 2025 releases removed from the analysis
- Final dataset contained approximately 15,000 films

### Variables Used

- Release year
- Budget (USD)
- Revenue (USD)
- Audience ratings

## Methodology

## Data Preparation

- Removed 2025 releases
- Cleaned and filtered movie records
- Grouped films into COVID periods

### COVID Periods

| Period     | Years     |
|------------|-----------|
| Pre-COVID  | 2016–2018 |
| COVID      | 2019–2021 |
| Post-COVID | 2022–2024 |

## Analysis

- Calculated mean budgets by year
- Calculated mean revenues by year
- Compared averages across periods
- Examined release volume trends

## Results: Budget and Revenue Trends {.smaller}

```{r}
#| label: fig-yearly
#| fig-cap: "Yearly mean budget and revenue for Netflix films, 2016–2023 (USD)."
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 7

library(tidyverse)

netflix <- read_csv("data/netflix_data.csv") |>
  filter(release_year >= 2016, release_year <= 2024,
         budget > 0, revenue > 0)

yearly <- netflix |>
  group_by(release_year) |>
  summarise(
    `Mean budget` = mean(budget, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Mean revenue` = mean(revenue, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(`Mean budget`, `Mean revenue`),
               names_to = "Measure", values_to = "USD")

ggplot(yearly, aes(x = release_year, y = USD, colour = Measure)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(2019, 2021), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey50") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar(scale = 1e-6,
                                                    suffix = "M")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Mean budget" = "#221F1F",
                                  "Mean revenue" = "#E50914")) +
  labs(x = "Release year", y = "Mean (USD)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

```

## Key Findings

- Revenue declined sharply at the beginning of the COVID period.
- Budgets remained relatively stable.
- Revenue recovered strongly after 2020.
- Budgets increased through 2021 before stabilising

## Results: Period Comparison

| Period     | Mean Budget | Mean Revenue |
|------------|-------------|--------------|
| Pre-COVID  | 35.0        | 117.4        |
| COVID      | 38.0        | 99.6         |
| Post-COVID | 43.1        | 107.3        |


*All figures in USD millions.*



### Key Takeaway
Budgets increased throughout the pandemic while revenues fell during COVID and only partially recovered afterwards.
